name: The Great Hall
firstVisit: Not a guard. Not a servant. Just the sound of your own feet, coming back to you from very far away.
At the far end, the doors to the throne room stand open.

=: A red carpet, all the way to the throne room. Nobody walks on it. You can tell.
I: A pillar of black stone, fluted, banded in gold. Somebody has carved a tally into the back of it. Days. Thousands of them.
4: The throne room. The doors stand open, as if you're expected.
1: The way back out to the grounds.
%: The foot of the winding stair. Up to the king's floor.
B: The fist crushing a crown. Underneath it, older stitching shows through: a different crest.
f: A portrait of Kaldor. Then you notice the one opposite. Each is more flattering than the last.
c: A torch in an iron bracket. The only warm thing in here.
A: An empty suit of armour on a stand. It's facing the door. They all are.
Z: A statue of Kaldor. A small one. By his standards.
W: Black stone, cold to the touch.
5: A portrait of a king, the face scratched out, very thoroughly.
The plaque reads OSRIC HALE. Somebody has added a word underneath, very neatly: MAD.
6: An old banner, almost hidden under the new one: an open hand, holding a sword by the blade. The crest of Halecrest, before it was the Berserker Kingdom.
7: A suit of armour, child-sized. Somebody has scratched a letter inside the collar: B.
8: A portrait of the old queen. Her face has been painted over.
Not scratched out, like the king's. Painted, carefully. As if someone wanted her forgotten, but politely.
9: A muster roll of the king's army. Ten thousand names.
Every one is crossed out, and written in again underneath, in different ink. Beside each, one word: RAISED.
0: A wizard's staff, snapped in three and mounted like a trophy. Under it, a plaque: SOON.
U: The winding stair: a round stone well of steps, turning up and up into the dark around a single black post. Somewhere above, people are laughing.
2: A doorway. Through it: clattering, shouting, and a smell of porridge. So that's where everyone is.
3: Steps going down, into the cold. Down there, something is standing very still. A lot of somethings.
H: A heavy door, shut. Behind it, low voices, and the scrape of something being pushed across a table.
